According to the National Institute of Health, the particles cause between 100,000 and 200,000 premature deaths each year

Data centers require vast amounts of power, and the influx of the complexes has caused some people’s energy bills to go up. With rising electric costs drawing public frustration, developers are beginning to pursue alternative power options, which can bring additional pollutants in turn.

The centers also cannot lose power without risking vast amounts of data, so they may rely on emergency backup generators. Many data centers use diesel generators as backup power, which are particularly strong polluters.
